title: RIROS: A Parallel RTL Fault SImulation FRamework with TwO-Dimensional Parallelism and Unified Schedule
evidence_span: The abstract identifies time-consuming RTL fault simulation, imbalanced fault-propagation tasks, two-dimensional structural-level and fault-level parallelism, work stealing, and unified computation/global synchronization scheduling; Table II supplies runtime comparisons with unresolved JPEG ratios.
problem: Dynamic fault propagation creates uneven RTL simulation tasks and idle cores.
method_or_artifact: Taskflow scheduling combines structural work stealing with fault-wise splitting of overloaded nodes; dependency-constrained local synchronization overlaps computation.
workload_or_benchmark: Seven RTL designs spanning RISC-V cores, accelerators and JPEG; stuck-at wire/register faults, with fault dropping disabled.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Reported Intel i7, 16 cores at 3.80GHz; C++ Taskflow, gcc-11 -O2; exact CPU SKU and VCS version unresolved.
limits: Headline metrics withheld: JPEG runtime ratios disagree with reported speedups. Cross-tool comparisons are not equal-core scaling. Correctness depends on preserving current-cycle reads before synchronization; no independent reproduction or safety certification.

evidence_locators.location: Section V; visually checked Table II PDF page 7; iccad/data/riros-primary-recovery-v1.json

title: Capacitance Extraction via Machine Learning with Application to Interconnect Geometry Exploration
evidence_span: The abstract reports that commercial parasitic extraction takes 25 minutes for a layer-thickness change, while the machine-learning method extracts standard-cell parasitic capacitance within seconds and predicts coupling capacitance for unseen layer thickness within milliseconds; Sections V–VI describe geometry features, field-solver labels, layer-specific regressors and thickness exploration.
problem: Repeated parasitic extraction makes standard-cell interconnect geometry exploration expensive.
method_or_artifact: Layout cross-sections feed layer-specific capacitance regressors trained on 2D field-solver labels; DNNs handle sensitive M0 cases and LightGBM handles others.
workload_or_benchmark: 94 standard cells in imec N2 predictive nanosheet PDK; M0-thickness sweep, not cross-library evaluation.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Dual Intel 6454S workstation with 89 training threads; predictive PDK, not measured silicon; inference timings exclude database construction and tuning.
limits: 38nm is described as unseen but used for hyperparameter-selection loss; untouched holdout not established. Boundary errors increase. Preparation/training costs must be amortized before asserting flow acceleration. No demonstrated cross-library transfer or independent acceptance.

evidence_locators.location: Sections VI.A–D; visually checked Table IV and Figures 14–16 PDF page 8; iccad/data/capacitance-ml-primary-recovery-v1.json
